title: Counting the added base
hook: Add base and watch the balance change.

knows: Strong acid and strong base react in a 1:1 acid–base ratio.
doesNotKnow: How excess reagent and total volume determine pH in this ideal model.

misconception: Equal volumes always imply equivalence, regardless of concentration.
objective: Use stoichiometry and the stated ideal approximation to interpret a strong-acid/base titration.

claims.text: Question, chart and reveal: An ideal 10 mL sample of 0.100 M HCl is mixed with 10 mL of 0.100 M NaOH at 25 °C. Assume complete reaction, additive volumes and concentration-based pH. How many millimoles of hydroxide were added? Initially there is 1.00 mmol acid; 10 mL of base adds 1.00 mmol hydroxide. Neither reactant is in stoichiometric excess. The final volume is 20 mL and the model pH is approximately 7.00. The model approximates activity by concentration.
claims.source: Strong-acid/base stoichiometry and concentration approximation; OpenStax https://openstax.org/books/chemistry-2e/pages/14-7-acid-base-titrations

claims.text: The beaker is a schematic model, not a laboratory procedure or literal particle count.
Recall: For this equal-molarity HCl–NaOH model, what addition makes acid and base amounts equal? 10 mL of 0.100 M base supplies 1.00 mmol hydroxide, equal to the original 1.00 mmol acid.

recall.question: For this equal-molarity HCl–NaOH model, what addition makes acid and base amounts equal?
recall.why: 10 mL of 0.100 M base supplies 1.00 mmol hydroxide, equal to the original 1.00 mmol acid.
